title: Ranveer Singh Turns 41. His Director Called His Performance 'Touched by Divine Grace.'
excerpt: Aditya Dhar's birthday tribute to Ranveer goes beyond industry niceties — it reads like a love letter from a filmmaker who watched an actor become transcendent.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Aditya Dhar praised Ranveer Singh's performance as 'touched by divine grace' on his 41st birthday.
  • The Dhurandhar duology grossed over ₹3,100 crore worldwide, showcasing Ranveer's box office power.
  • Ranveer's portrayal in Dhurandhar is considered one of the finest in Indian cinema history.
  • Tributes from industry peers highlight Ranveer's impact and camaraderie on set.
  • Ranveer's next project, Pralay, is set to begin shooting in August 2026.

There are birthday posts, and then there's what Aditya Dhar wrote for Ranveer Singh on Sunday.

The filmmaker behind the Dhurandhar duology — the most commercially successful back-to-back films in Indian cinema history — took to social media as Ranveer turned 41, sharing behind-the-scenes photographs from the sets and writing the kind of tribute that stops you mid-scroll.

> "Some films stay with you forever. Dhurandhar will always be one of those films for me. Not just because of the story we told but because I got to witness something very few directors ever get to witness."

What followed was a scene-by-scene appreciation of Ranveer's work — the 26/11 sequence, the Pathankot massacre, the final tea shop scene, the pump house scene, the court exterior — each one called out as a moment where the actor reached something elemental.

> "Every emotion landed exactly where it needed to. Every silence had meaning. Every glance had intent. Every beat was pitch perfect."

> ""To more fabulous memories, performances, successes, love, ice baths, laughs, celebrations," Rampal wrote."

Dhar described the performance as "one of the finest Indian cinema has ever seen" and called it "a force of nature that completely disappeared into the soul of the character." And then the note shifted from professional admiration to something more personal: "Somewhere along the way, you stopped being just my actor. You became my brother."

The Numbers Behind the Bond

![Aditya Dhar — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Aditya_Dhar_at_IFFI_2019_%28cropped%29.jpg)

This isn't just sentiment — it's backed by staggering commercial proof. The first Dhurandhar, released in December 2025, grossed over ₹1,300 crore worldwide. Its sequel, Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge, released in March 2026, went even bigger — crossing ₹1,800 crore globally.

Combined, the duology has earned over ₹3,100 crore worldwide, placing Ranveer Singh firmly alongside Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan in the rarefied tier of Bollywood actors who can open a ₹1,000-crore film. At 41, he may well be the most bankable leading man in Indian cinema right now.

The Industry Celebrates

Ranveer's birthday brought tributes from across the film fraternity. Arjun Rampal, who played the chilling ISI officer Major Iqbal in the Dhurandhar films, posted a behind-the-scenes video montage from the sets — candid laughs between takes, raw performance clips, and a sketch of Ranveer's character. "To more fabulous memories, performances, successes, love, ice baths, laughs, celebrations," Rampal wrote. His partner Gabriella Demetriades added her own birthday wishes in the comments.

In the Dhurandhar films, Ranveer plays Jaskirat Singh Rangi, an undercover Indian intelligence officer operating under the deep-cover identity of Hamza Ali Mazari. It's a role that required him to oscillate between vulnerability and controlled violence — a performance that clearly left its mark on everyone involved.

What's Next: Pralay and Beyond

Reports indicate that Ranveer's next major project, Pralay, begins shooting in August 2026. Meanwhile, his frequent collaborator Vicky Kaushal has reportedly blocked 18 months for the ambitious mythological epic Mahavatar. The two actors represent the most commercially potent generation of Bollywood leading men since the Khans — and both are making choices that suggest they're thinking in franchises, not films.

Dhar, for his part, confirmed that he and Ranveer are "planning another film together next year." Given that their first two collaborations earned a combined ₹3,100 crore, that's less an announcement than a foregone conclusion.

The Transformation That Matters

What makes Ranveer's current moment remarkable is the distance he's travelled. The man who broke through with Band Baaja Baaraat in 2010 — charming, electric, impossible to look away from — has become something more formidable. The Dhurandhar role demanded stillness, restraint, and the kind of interior work that the industry once reserved for a different generation of actors.

At 41, Ranveer Singh isn't just a movie star. He's the actor his generation needed to become. And if Aditya Dhar's birthday note is any indication, the people who've worked closest with him know it best.
